newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Netanyahu calls a meeting and ministers show up.
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu calls a meeting and ministers show up.

text.p: Israel's beleaguered leader Benjamin Netanyahu scored a political victory on Friday -- he held a cabinet meeting and no one boycotted.
"There seems to be perfect harmony. The whole meeting was very routine," Netanyahu's communications adviser David Bar-Illan told Reuters.
Each of the past two weeks at least one disgruntled cabinet minister had pointedly failed to show up.
"(Justice Minister) Tsahi Hanegbi was a little late but that was presumably due to oversleeping," Bar-Illan said.
The successful meeting came days after Netanyahu narrowly survived a parliamentary no-confidence vote in which one-sixth of his coalition partners failed to support the government.
But the prime minister has not yet hacked his way out of the political weeds. His fractious cabinet is still squabbling over a ministerial shake-up expected next week.

Political analysts said Foreign Minister David Levy and Yitzhak Mordechai opposed giving hawkish ex-general Ariel Sharon, tipped to be finance minister, a place on Netanyahu's inner team which hashes out Arab-Israeli peace strategy.
Netanyahu has been plagued by political defections within his own Likud party and ministers have voiced concern over his handling of government.
"I presume we'll have a cabinet in place by Monday," Bar-Illan said.
